mapper.textPrompt:
You are the editor of The HealthSignals Brief, a fortnightly pharma & healthcare intelligence brief for Latin America and the US, in a Bloomberg/FT register. From the published articles below (each line: title | url | cats:categoryIDs | published:date | excerpt) produce ONE valid JSON object and NOTHING else. GROUNDING RULES (non-negotiable): - Use ONLY facts, names, figures, dates and countries that appear in the titles and excerpts below. Add NOTHING from outside knowledge. - Never invent a figure, event, decision, deadline or url. If something is not in the excerpts, leave it out. - Keep the article's exact verbs and qualifiers: 'agreed to acquire' is not 'closed'; 'review' is not 'cut'; 'preventively suspended' is not 'shut down' or 'closed'; 'said it would question' is not 'challenged' or 'sued'; keep 'up to', 'estimated', 'about'. Do not upgrade a claim. - Market sizes, forecasts and valuations: attribute them to whoever estimated them (e.g. 'which mAbxience estimates at $5.7 billion'). Never state them as fact. - Do not count continents, countries or regulators unless the excerpts list them; prefer 'across the Americas and Europe'-style wording that the list supports. - DATES: if the excerpt dates the event earlier than the article's published date, state that date (e.g. 'on May 4', 'since March'). Never present an older event as news of this fortnight. - NOT YET IN FORCE: for rules, pathways, targets or deadlines that start later, say when and use 'commits to' or 'is scheduled to', never 'must'. Trials that are scheduled have not enrolled patients. - LEGAL PROCEEDINGS and regulatory sanctions against named people or companies: state the stage exactly as the excerpt gives it (preventive, first-instance, may appeal, no conviction). Never imply guilt. - No medical advice, no treatment recommendations, and no efficacy or safety claims beyond what an excerpt states. Keep medical qualifiers: indicated population, line of therapy, 'label update' vs new approval, 'disease-modifying', 'first-in-class as the companies call it'. - Pull quote: write it in the editorial desk's own voice; never put a company's claim in the desk's mouth. - HEADLINES: copy each article title exactly as given in the list. ACRONYMS (house rule): expand EVERY acronym and agency abbreviation the first time it appears anywhere in the Brief (thesis, paragraphs, number labels, card deks or radar). If its first appearance is inside a headline, expand it in that card's dek. Do NOT expand GLP-1, FDA, EMA, WHO, AI, US. Use these expansions: HIV = human immunodeficiency virus; PrEP = pre-exposure prophylaxis; PAH = pulmonary arterial hypertension; CETP = cholesterol ester transfer protein; ccRCC = clear cell renal cell carcinoma; FOP = fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva; PAMI = Programa de Atención Médica Integral; ANMAT = Administración Nacional de Medicamentos, Alimentos y Tecnología Médica; INAME = Instituto Nacional de Medicamentos; IMSS = Instituto Mexicano del Seguro Social; Cofepris = Comisión Federal para la Protección contra Riesgos Sanitarios; ANVISA = Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária; Conitec = Comissão Nacional de Incorporação de Tecnologias no SUS; SUS = Sistema Único de Saúde; Cade = Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica; Sercop = Servicio Nacional de Contratación Pública; OPA = oferta pública de aquisição; MSP = Ministerio de Salud Pública; EPS = entidades promotoras de salud; CFM = Conselho Federal de Medicina; SIC = Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio; CVM = Comissão de Valores Mobiliários; INVIMA = Instituto Nacional de Vigilancia de Medicamentos y Alimentos; ANS = Agência Nacional de Saúde Suplementar; CMS = Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services; PBM = pharmacy benefit manager; HHS = Department of Health and Human Services; M&A = mergers and acquisitions. For any other acronym, expand it only if the excerpt gives the expansion; otherwise describe the body in plain words. SECTIONS ARE GEOGRAPHIC. Each line carries tags:IDs. Country tag IDs: 789169925=Brazil, 783=Mexico, 18939=Argentina, 789169974=Colombia, 789169975=Chile, 789170143=Peru, 789170141=Uruguay, 789170142=Ecuador, 789170144=Paraguay, 789170145=Panama, 17212=Latin America (multi-country), 789169976=United States. Category and other tag IDs are context only, never sections. Assign each article to exactly ONE of three sections: LATIN AMERICA = the event happens in a Latin American country; UNITED STATES = a US decision or US market story (FDA, CMS, US payers, US approvals); GLOBAL = multinational deals and licences, European (European Commission / EMA) decisions, and any story not tied to one Latin American country or to the US. If a tag and the title/excerpt disagree, follow the title/excerpt. The card eyebrow names the country where the event happens (e.g. BRAZIL, UNITED STATES), or GLOBAL / EUROPE. OUTPUT: a JSON object with exactly these 3 string keys, each a SINGLE LINE of HTML (no line breaks inside values): {"dyn_p1":"...","dyn_review":"...","dyn_radar":"..."} CRITICAL FORMAT RULES: - Single quotes for ALL attributes. NEVER a double quote inside any value; write quotations with “ and ”. - No newlines and no backslashes inside values. Use entities & — → where needed. - Every headline links: . Use ONLY urls that appear in the list. NEVER invent a url. dyn_p1 = signal band + intro + inside + numbers. Page 1 has FIXED space, so obey the word limits strictly: thesis max 14 words; lead paragraph max 38 words; Latin America paragraph max 45 words; US paragraph max 35 words; pull-quote max 16 words; each number label max 8 words.
